# nativeDragZone can only read DOM attributes, so a business id forces useInternalId: false

## Context

`Neo.component.Base#nativeDragZone` (#17885) lets a component declare a native drag payload as JSON, which `Neo.main.addon.NativeDragSource` turns into a real `DataTransfer` on the main thread. The declaration is a template map — `{'text/plain': 'app:{data-record-id}'}` — and `NativeDragSource.mjs:183` resolves every token through exactly one source:

```js
dataTransfer.setData(type, template.replace(templateToken, (match, name) => node.getAttribute(name) ?? ''))
```

`getAttribute`, and nothing else. That is deliberate — the class comment says so, and it is what keeps the declaration JSON-safe across the worker boundary.

The consequence is a coupling nobody declared: **to put a business id on the clipboard, the business id must first be written into the DOM.** For a grid that means `useInternalId: false`, because otherwise `Neo.grid.Body#getRecordId` writes neo's own `neo-record-N` and the payload carries it instead.

Verified live on `dev` this session by driving a real browser drag into a real same-origin iframe: `childDragEnter 1`, `drop` fired, and both `text/plain` and the custom MIME arrived carrying the attribute value. The mechanism works. The coupling is what this ticket is about.

## The Problem

**The failure is silent.** With `useInternalId: true` and an attribute template naming the record-id attribute, there is no error, no warning, and no signal anywhere. `getAttribute` returns `neo-record-7`, `setData` accepts it, the drag runs, the drop fires, and the receiver looks up an id that does not exist in its domain — so nothing happens. The gesture completes successfully and does nothing, which is the hardest class of defect to attribute to its cause.

**The pairing is enforced only by prose.** Two JSDoc blocks describe it. Nothing mechanical checks it. A grid can be given a `nativeDragZone` today, or have `useInternalId` flipped tomorrow, and both edits look locally correct.

**`useInternalId` is not a free knob to switch off.** `internalId` was adopted deliberately for stable DOM keying across grid, table, list and data views (#9070, #9071, #9072), and the record-resolution paths in the selection models, `grid.Body#getRecord`, `getRecordFromLogicalId` and `list` `DragZone` were all reworked to resolve through it. Requiring `useInternalId: false` asks a consumer to opt out of that architecture in order to use an unrelated feature — a drag concern reaching back into DOM identity.

**Why the obvious fix does not work.** The authoritative record lives in the app-worker store; the `DataTransfer` must be filled **synchronously** inside the main thread's `dragstart` handler. There is no time to ask the app worker anything. That is precisely why the current implementation reads attributes: the DOM is the only thing the main thread already has.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/main/addon/NativeDragSource.mjs` — `templateToken = /\{([\w-]+)\}/g` (`:8`); the single resolution site is `:183`; `register({ownerId, delegate, types, effectAllowed})` (`:249`) is the whole registration contract and carries no record data.
- `src/component/Base.mjs` — `nativeDragZone_` (`:209`), `afterSetNativeDragZone` (`:647`), and the generation-guarded push to the addon (`:664-676`). The declaration already re-issues on change, so a registration payload that carries more than templates has a delivery path that exists.
- `src/grid/Body.mjs` — `getRecordId` is what writes `neo-record-N` when `useInternalId` is true.
- The synchronous constraint is real and is the design's reason for existing; any fix must respect it by pushing data to main **ahead** of `dragstart`, never fetching at `dragstart`.

## The Fix

Give a template a second resolution source that does not require the value to be in the DOM: let a token resolve a **record field**, with the mapping delivered to the main thread as part of the registration.

1. Extend the `nativeDragZone` declaration with an explicit record-field form, distinguishable from an attribute token at parse time (so existing attribute templates keep their exact meaning — no reinterpretation of `{data-record-id}`).
2. The owning component pushes a node-id → field-value map alongside the registration and refreshes it when the underlying rows change, so `NativeDragSource` holds the values **before** any `dragstart` and stays synchronous at resolution time.
3. Resolution falls back to `getAttribute` when a token is not a declared field, preserving today's behaviour for every current consumer.
4. A grid declaring a `nativeDragZone` no longer needs `useInternalId: false`; the two settings become independent.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `component.Base#nativeDragZone` declaration | #17885; `src/component/Base.mjs:209` | gains an explicit record-field token form beside the existing attribute form | an undeclared token resolves via `getAttribute`, exactly as today | `nativeDragZone_` JSDoc + `NativeDragSource` class comment | positive: a field token yields the store value with `useInternalId: true`; negative: an unknown token still yields the attribute, and an absent attribute still yields `''` |
| `NativeDragSource.register({ownerId, delegate, types, effectAllowed})` (`:249`) | `src/main/addon/NativeDragSource.mjs:249` | accepts the field-value map; resolution at `:183` consults it before `getAttribute` | registrations without the map behave identically to today | addon class comment | a registration omitting the map drives an unchanged drag |
| the `useInternalId: false` pairing | prose only, in two JSDoc blocks | retired — the settings become independent | n/a | both JSDoc blocks updated to stop prescribing the pairing | a grid with `useInternalId: true` + a field token puts the business id on the clipboard |
| the synchronous `dragstart` contract | `NativeDragSource` design (#17885) | unchanged — values are pushed on register/update, never fetched at `dragstart` | none; a fetch at `dragstart` is the defect being avoided | addon class comment | no `await` on the `dragstart` path; the map is read from memory |

## Decision Record impact

`none` — this extends a component/main-thread addon contract inside its existing ownership. It does not touch `ai/`, so §1c Agent OS Structure Map is **N/A**.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 A `nativeDragZone` template can name a record field, and the resulting `DataTransfer` carries the store value while the owning grid has `useInternalId: true`. Red-first: the same declaration on `dev` puts `neo-record-N` on the clipboard.
- [ ] AC-2 Control — an existing attribute-token declaration is byte-identical in behaviour: same MIME types, same values, no registration change required.
- [ ] AC-3 Control — an unresolvable token still yields `''` rather than the literal template text, matching `?? ''` today.
- [ ] AC-4 The `dragstart` path performs no asynchronous work: the field values are present in the addon before the gesture begins, and a spec asserts the resolution site reads only from memory.
- [ ] AC-5 The values survive a row update — changing the underlying record and dragging again yields the new value, not a stale one captured at first registration.
- [ ] AC-6 Both JSDoc blocks stop prescribing `useInternalId: false`, and a grid pairing `useInternalId: true` with a field token is exercised by a spec.

## Out of Scope

- **The interim dev-mode guard.** A cheaper mitigation exists: warn when a `nativeDragZone` template references the record-id attribute while the owning body has `useInternalId: true`. It makes the silent class loud without removing the coupling. Deliberately not bundled — if this ticket slips, that guard is worth filing on its own, but shipping both means building a warning for a coupling this ticket deletes.
- Changing any default: `useInternalId` keeps its current default, and no existing consumer is migrated by this work.
- The payload protocol itself (which MIME types, what prefix). That is the receiving application's contract, not the engine's.
- The synthetic drag pipeline (`draggable/`), which is a separate mechanism from native `DataTransfer`.

## Avoided Traps

- **Resolving the record at `dragstart`.** The obvious shape — ask the app worker for the record when the drag starts — cannot work: `DataTransfer` must be filled synchronously inside the handler, and the store lives in another thread. Any prescription that reaches across the worker boundary at gesture time is wrong by construction. The data must already be on main.
- **Reinterpreting the existing token syntax.** Making `{foo}` mean "field `foo`, else attribute `foo`" would silently change the meaning of every shipped declaration the first time a field and an attribute share a name. The field form must be explicit at parse time.
- **"Just document the pairing harder."** It is already documented in two places, and prose did not prevent the class — the failure mode is silent, so a consumer gets no feedback that they read the docs wrong.
- **Treating this as a grid ticket.** The coupling lives in the resolution rule, not in the grid. Any component with a `nativeDragZone` whose meaningful id is not already a DOM attribute has the same problem; the grid is simply where it was observed.

## Consumer census, corrected: four declaring grids, not one — all four correctly paired

I said in the ticket body and the A2A that the downstream consumer workspace has **one** declaring grid. That was wrong, and the way it was wrong is worth recording because it is the same instrument failure twice.

**The correct census.** Four `nativeDragZone` declarations across three widgets, in **two different nested repositories** of that workspace:

| declaration | pairing | same config object? |
|---|---|---|
| widget A, grid 1 | `body: {module: GridBody, selectionModel: CellRowModel, useInternalId: false}` | yes — `columns:` follows, no intervening close |
| widget A, grid 2 | `body: {useInternalId: false}` | yes — adjacent lines |
| widget B | `body: {useInternalId: false}` | yes — adjacent lines |
| widget C (the other repository) | `body: {selectionModel: CellRowModel, useInternalId: false}` | yes — `reference`/`columns` siblings, no intervening close |

**4/4 correctly paired.** Adjacency was checked per declaration rather than inferred from both tokens appearing in one file — a declaration and a `useInternalId: false` in the same file can belong to different grids, and that distinction is the whole question. So nothing on the demo path carries a `neo-record-N` payload, and this ticket remains a class fix rather than an incident.

**Why my count was wrong — two instrument failures, both silent:**

1. **`--exclude-dir` placed after the search path.** `grep -RIn 'tok' "$ROOT" --exclude-dir=node_modules` returned **zero matches and exit 0** on a tree that demonstrably contains the token. Options after the operand are not parsed as options here. The failure produces an empty result set, not an error — indistinguishable from a true absence.
2. **Seven nested git repositories.** The workspace root contains its own `.git` plus six inner repositories. A `git grep` from the outer root sees **none** of the inner trees' files, and the real consumers live in two inner repositories my first search never entered. `git grep` also reported zero, cleanly.

Both instruments answered "absent" for a thing that was present four times. What caught it was a positive control: `grep -c` on a file I had already read by other means returned 1 while the recursive search returned nothing, which cannot both be true. The working instrument was `find … -prune -o -type f -print | xargs grep -n`.

The generalizable bit, which applies to any consumer-impact claim in this ticket: **an empty search over a multi-repo workspace is not evidence of absence until a positive control proves the search could have found something.** Anyone sizing the migration surface for this change should enumerate the nested repositories first.

🖖 Grace
